title: 师说
author: 韩愈
content: 古之学者必有师。师者，所以传道受业解惑也。人非生而知之者，孰能无惑？惑而不从师，其为惑也，终不解矣。生乎吾前，其闻道也固先乎吾，吾从而师之；生乎吾后，其闻道也亦先乎吾，吾从而师之。吾师道也，夫庸知其年之先后生于吾乎？是故无贵无贱，无长无少，道之所存，师之所存也。嗟乎！师道之不传也久矣！欲人之无惑也难矣！古之圣人，其出人也远矣，犹且从师而问焉；今之众人，其下圣人也亦远矣，而耻学于师。是故圣益圣，愚益愚。圣人之所以为圣，愚人之所以为愚，其皆出于此乎？爱其子，择师而教之；于其身也，则耻师焉，惑矣。彼童子之师，授之书而习其句读者，非吾所谓传其道解其惑者也。句读之不知，惑之不解，或师焉，或不（fǒu）焉，小学而大遗，吾未见其明也。巫医乐师百工之人，不耻相师。士大夫之族，曰师曰弟子云者，则群聚而笑之。问之，则曰：“彼与彼年相若也，何资格而师之？” 呜呼！师道之不复，可知矣。巫医乐师百工之人，君子不齿，今其智乃反不能及，其可怪也欤！圣人无常师。孔子师郯子、苌弘、师襄、老聃。郯子之徒，其贤不及孔子。孔子曰：“三人行，则必有我师。” 是故弟子不必不如师，师不必贤于弟子，闻道有先后，术业有专攻，如是而已。李氏子蟠，年十七，好古文，六艺经传皆通习之，不拘于时，来问于我。余嘉其能行古道，作《师说》以贻之。
pinyin: gǔ zhī xué zhě bì yǒu shī。shī zhě，suǒ yǐ chuán dào shòu yè jiě huò yě。rén fēi shēng ér zhī zhī zhě，shú néng wú huò？huò ér bù cóng shī，qí wèi huò yě，zhōng bù jiě yǐ。shēng hū wú qián，qí wén dào yě gù xiān hū wú，wú cóng ér shī zhī；shēng hū wú hòu，qí wén dào yě yì xiān hū wú，wú cóng ér shī zhī。wú shī dào yě，fū yōng zhī qí nián zhī xiān hòu shēng yú wú hū？shì gù wú guì wú jiàn，wú cháng wú shǎo，dào zhī suǒ cún，shī zhī suǒ cún yě。jiē hū！shī dào zhī bù chuán yě jiǔ yǐ！yù rén zhī wú huò yě nán yǐ！gǔ zhī shèng rén，qí chū rén yě yuǎn yǐ，yóu qiě cóng shī ér wèn yān；jīn zhī zhòng rén，qí xià shèng rén yě yì yuǎn yǐ，ér chǐ xué yú shī。shì gù shèng yì shèng，yú yì yú。shèng rén zhī suǒ yǐ wéi shèng，yú rén zhī suǒ yǐ wéi yú，qí jiē chū yú cǐ hū？ài qí zǐ，zé shī ér jiào zhī；yú qí shēn yě，则 chǐ shī yān，huò yǐ。bǐ tóng zǐ zhī shī，shòu zhī shū ér xí qí jù dú zhě，fēi wú suǒ wèi chuán qí dào jiě qí huò zhě yě。jù dú zhī bù zhī，huò zhī bù jiě，huò shī yān，huò fǒu yān，xiǎo xué ér dà yí，wú wèi jiàn qí míng yě。wū yī yuè shī bǎi gōng zhī rén，bù chǐ xiāng shī。shì dà fū zhī zú，yuē shī yuē dì zǐ yún zhě，则 qún jù ér xiào zhī。wèn zhī，则 yuē：“bǐ yǔ bǐ nián xiāng ruò yě，yǐ hé zī gé ér shī zhī？”wū hū！shī dào zhī bù fù，kě zhī yǐ。wū yī yuè shī bǎi gōng zhī rén，jūn zǐ bù chǐ，jīn qí zhì nǎi fǎn bù néng jí，qí kě guài yě yú！shèng rén wú cháng shī。kǒng zǐ shī tán zǐ、cháng hóng、shī xiāng、lǎo dān。tán zǐ zhī tú，qí xián bù jí kǒng zǐ。kǒng zǐ yuē：“sān rén xíng，则 bì yǒu wǒ shī。”shì gù dì zǐ bù bì bù rú shī，shī bù bì xián yú dì zǐ，wén dào yǒu xiān hòu，shù yè yǒu zhuān gōng，rú shì ér yǐ。lǐ shì zǐ pán，nián shí qī，hào gǔ wén，liù yì jīng zhuàn jiē tōng xí zhī，bù jū yú shí，lái wèn yú wǒ。yú jiā qí néng xíng gǔ dào，zuò《shī shuō》yǐ yí zhī。

annotations.zh: 学者：求学的人。师者，所以传道受业解惑也：老师，是用来传授道理、教授学业、解答疑难问题的人。受，通 “授”。之：指知识和道理。孰：谁。生乎吾前：在我之前出生。乎，相当于 “于”。闻：知道，懂得。从而师之：跟从（他），拜他为老师。师道：从师的风尚。庸：岂，哪。是故：因此。无：无论。嗟乎：叹词。众人：一般人。下：低于。耻：以…… 为耻。圣益圣：圣人更加圣明。益，更加。愚人：愚昧的人。其：大概。身：自己。惑矣：糊涂啊。句读（dòu）：也叫句逗，古人指文辞休止和停顿处。或：有的。不（fǒu）：通 “否”。小学：小的方面学习。遗：丢弃。巫医：古代巫和医不分。乐师：以演奏音乐为职业的人。百工：各种工匠。相师：互相学习。士大夫：指官吏或有声望、地位的知识分子。族：类。笑之：讥笑他们。彼：他。年相若：年龄差不多。以：凭借。乃：竟然。常师：固定的老师。郯（tán）子：春秋时郯国的国君苌弘：周敬王时的大夫。师襄：春秋时鲁国的乐官。老聃（dān）：即老子。之徒：这些人。贤：才德。不必：不一定。术业：学问和技艺。专攻：专门研究。李氏子蟠：李家的孩子名蟠。六艺：《诗》《书》《礼》《乐》《易》《春秋》六种经书。经传：经文和传文。拘：限制。时：时俗。嘉：赞许。古道：古人从师之道。贻：赠送。
annotations.en: Scholars in ancient times must have teachers. Teachers are those who pass on the truth, impart knowledge and solve doubts. 'Shou' here is equivalent to 'Shou' in modern Chinese which means to teach. 'Zhi' refers to knowledge and truth. 'Shu' means who. 'Sheng hu wu qian' means being born before me. 'Hu' is equivalent to 'Yu'. 'Wen' means to know and understand. 'Cong er shi zhi' means to follow (him) and make him a teacher. 'Shi dao' refers to the custom of learning from teachers. 'Yong' means how could. 'Shi gu' means therefore. 'Wu' means regardless of. 'Jie hu' is an interjection. 'Zhong ren' refers to ordinary people. 'Xia' means lower than. 'Chi' means regarding... as shameful. 'Sheng yi sheng' means sages are more sage. 'Yi' means more. 'Yu ren' means foolish people. 'Qi' probably. 'Shen' means oneself. 'Huo yi' means confused. 'Ju dou' also called sentence and pause, refers to the place where ancient people's words stop and pause. 'Huo' means some. 'Fou' is equivalent to 'Fou' in modern Chinese which means not. 'Xiao xue' means learning in small aspects. 'Yi' means discarding. 'Wu yi' in ancient times, witchcraft and medicine were not separated. 'Yue shi' refers to those who make a living by playing music. 'Bai gong' refers to various craftsmen. 'Xiang shi' means learning from each other. 'Shi da fu' refers to officials or intellectuals with prestige and status. 'Zu' means kind. 'Xiao zhi' means laughing at them. 'Bi' means he. 'Nian xiang ruo' means of similar age. 'Yi' means by. 'Nai' means unexpectedly. 'Chang shi' means fixed teachers. 'Tan zi' was the monarch of the state of Tan during the Spring and Autumn Period. 'Chang hong' was a doctor during the reign of King Jing of Zhou. 'Shi xiang' was a music official in the state of Lu during the Spring and Autumn Period. 'Lao dan' is Laozi. 'Zhi tu' means these people. 'Xian' means virtue and talent. 'Bu bi' means not necessarily. 'Shu ye' means knowledge and skills. 'Zhuan gong' means specialized research. 'Li shi zi pan' means a child named Pan of the Li family. 'Liu yi' refers to six Confucian classics including 'The Book of Songs', 'The Book of History', 'The Book of Rites', 'The Book of Music', 'The Book of Changes' and 'The Spring and Autumn Annals'. 'Jing zhuan' refers to scriptures and commentaries. 'Ju' means to be restricted. 'Shi' means custom. 'Jia' means to praise. 'Gu dao' refers to the ancient way of learning from teachers. 'Yi' means to present.

appreciations.中文: 《师说》是一篇论述从师学习的重要性的文章。文章开篇提出‘古之学者必有师’，明确指出从师的必要性，接着阐述老师的职责是‘传道受业解惑’。然后通过对比古之圣人和今之众人、对其子与对自身、巫医乐师百工之人和士大夫之族的不同态度，批判了当时社会上耻于从师的不良风气。文中强调了从师不论贵贱长少，道之所存，师之所存。又以孔子从师为例，进一步说明弟子不必不如师，师不必贤于弟子，闻道有先后，术业有专攻的观点，鼓励人们积极从师学习，打破门第观念。全文逻辑严密，对比鲜明，具有很强的说服力。
appreciations.英文: On Teachers is an article discussing the importance of learning from teachers. At the beginning of the article, it is proposed that 'Scholars in ancient times must have teachers', clearly pointing out the necessity of learning from teachers. Then it elaborates that the duty of teachers is 'to pass on the truth, impart knowledge and solve doubts'. Then, by comparing the different attitudes of ancient sages and modern people, of people towards their children and themselves, of witches, doctors, musicians, craftsmen and the gentry, it criticizes the bad atmosphere of being ashamed of learning from teachers in society at that time. The article emphasizes that when it comes to learning from teachers, there is no distinction between noble and humble, old and young. Where there is truth, there are teachers. Taking Confucius' learning from teachers as an example, it further illustrates the view that disciples are not necessarily inferior to teachers, and teachers are not necessarily superior to disciples. People learn the truth earlier or later, and have specialized knowledge and skills, encouraging people to actively learn from teachers and break the concept of family status. The whole article is logically rigorous, with sharp contrasts and strong persuasiveness.

interpretations.中文: 古代求学的人一定有老师。老师，是（可以）依靠来传授道理、教授学业、解答疑难问题的。人不是生下来就懂得道理的，谁能没有疑惑？（有了）疑惑，如果不跟从老师（学习），那些成为疑难问题的，就最终不能理解了。生在我前面，他懂得道理本来就早于我，我（应该）跟从（他）把他当作老师；生在我后面，（如果）他懂得道理也早于我，我（也应该）跟从（他）把他当作老师。我（是向他）学习道理啊，哪管他的生年比我早还是比我晚呢？因此，无论地位高低贵贱，无论年纪大小，道理存在的地方，就是老师存在的地方。唉，（古代）从师（学习）的风尚不流传已经很久了，想要人没有疑惑难啊！古代的圣人，他们超出一般人很远，尚且跟从老师而请教；现在的一般人，他们（的才智）低于圣人很远，却以向老师学习为耻。因此圣人就更加圣明，愚人就更加愚昧。圣人之所以能成为圣人，愚人之所以能成为愚人，大概都出于这个原因吧？（人们）爱他们的孩子，就选择老师来他，（但是）对于他自己呢，却以跟从老师（学习）为可耻，真是糊涂啊！那些孩子们的老师，是教他们读书，（帮助他们）学习断句的，不是我所说的能传授那些道理，解答那些疑难问题的。（一方面）不通晓句读，（另一方面）不能解决疑惑，有的（句读）向老师学习，有的（疑惑）却不向老师学习；小的方面倒要学习，大的方面反而放弃（不学），我没看出那种人是明智的。巫医、乐师、各种工匠这些人，不以互相学习为耻。士大夫这类人，（听到）称 “老师” 称 “弟子” 的，就成群聚在一起讥笑人家。问他们（为什么讥笑），就说：“他和他年龄差不多，道德学问也差不多，（以）什么身份（资格）去当老师呢？” 唉！（古代那种）跟从老师学习的好风尚不能恢复，（从这些话里就）可以明白了。巫医、乐师、各种工匠这些人，君子们不屑一提，现在他们的见识竟反而赶不上（这些人），真是令人奇怪啊！圣人没有固定的老师。孔子曾以郯子、苌弘、师襄、老聃为师。郯子这些人，他们的贤能都比不上孔子。孔子说：“几个人一起走，（其中）一定有（可以当）我的老师（的人）。” 因此学生不一定不如师，老师不一定比学生贤能，听到的道理有早有晚，学问技艺各有专长，如此罢了。李家的孩子蟠，年龄十七，喜欢古文，六经的经文和传文都普遍地学习了，不受时俗的拘束，来向我请教。我赞许他能够遵行古人（从师）的途径，写这篇《师说》来赠送给他。
interpretations.英文: Scholars in ancient times surely had teachers. Teachers are those from whom one can learn the truth, acquire knowledge and get doubts solved. People are not born with knowledge of the truth. Who can be free of doubts? If one has doubts but doesn't learn from teachers, those doubts will never be solved. Those born before me knew the truth earlier than I. I should follow them and regard them as teachers. Those born after me, if they knew the truth earlier than I, I should also follow them and regard them as teachers. I learn from them because of the truth they know. Why should I care whether they are older or younger than I? Therefore, whether one is noble or humble, old or young, where the truth exists, there are teachers. Alas, the custom of learning from teachers has not been passed down for a long time. It's difficult to make people free of doubts. Ancient sages were far superior to ordinary people, yet they still learned from teachers and asked questions. Ordinary people nowadays are far inferior to sages in intelligence, but they are ashamed of learning from teachers. So sages become more sage, and fools become more foolish. The reason why sages are sages and fools are fools probably lies in this. People love their children and choose teachers to teach them. But for themselves, they are ashamed of learning from teachers. How foolish! The teachers of children teach them to read and learn punctuation, not those who can teach the truth and solve doubts as I mentioned. On the one hand, some people don't know punctuation; on the other hand, they can't solve doubts. They learn punctuation from teachers, but don't learn to solve doubts from teachers. They study minor things but give up major ones. I dont see the wisdom in this. People such as witches, doctors, musicians, and craftsmen are not ashamed of learning from each other. Among the scholar - officials, when they hear someone being called 'teacher' or 'disciple', they gather in groups and laugh at them. When asked why, they say, 'They are about the same age and have similar moral knowledge. On what basis can one be a teacher?' Alas! The good custom of learning from teachers in ancient times can't be restored, which can be understood from these remarks. People like witches, doctors, musicians, and craftsmen are despised by gentlemen. Now, their knowledge is unexpectedly inferior to those people. How strange! Sages have no fixed teachers. Confucius once took Tanzi, Changhong, Shixiang, and Laodan as his teachers. People like Tanzi are not as virtuous as Confucius. Confucius said, 'When several people walk together, there must be someone who can be my teacher among them.' Therefore, disciples are not necessarily inferior to teachers, and teachers are not necessarily more virtuous than disciples. People learn the truth earlier or later, and have their own specializations in knowledge and skills. That's all. Li Pan, a seventeen - year - old boy, loves ancient literature. He has studied the scriptures and commentaries of the Six Classics comprehensively. He is not restricted by the current customs and comes to consult me. I praise him for being able to follow the ancient way of learning from teachers. So I write this On Teachers to present to him.
